newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINES STOPS OFFER OF SHORT-TERM T-BILLS.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINES STOPS OFFER OF SHORT-TERM T-BILLS.

text.p: The Philippine Bureau of Treasury said on Wednesday it decided to stop offering 35-day and 42-day Treasury bills next week, a ranking official said on Wednesday.
"We are comfortable with the level of interest rates. We believe we can discontinue the short-term bills and reintroduce the Treasury bonds," Treasury director Juanchito Dispo told Reuters.
The short-term bills were introduced four weeks ago after the peso depreciated sharply and domestic interest rates shot up. It did not offer Treasury bonds during the period due to the high rates.
The Treasury is scheduled to re-offer five-year bonds on August 26, Dispo said.
Dispo also said the Bureau had raised the weekly T-bill offering to five billion pesos on Monday from four billion pesos.
Offering for the 364-day bills will be increased to two billion pesos from one billion pesos this week.
Volume for the 91-day and 182-day bills will remain at 1.5 billion pesos each.
Treasury bills fell steeply on Monday with the benchmark 91-day rate shedding more than 80 basis points.
